states: Actual production Docs/router/Markdown/styles render the exact served guide, with source-matching consuming fetch ArrayBuffer bytes in both engines.
Saved exact-ID confirmation, private credential/TLS reuse, refusal-preserved recovery and already-removed-service caution.
Credential-free repeated local cleanup is not revocation; older prepared scripts can still erase after a failed server notification.
interactions: 28 assertions across light desktop Chromium and dark phone WebKit; private-file removal command, readable refusal/recovery text and no page horizontal overflow.
Desktop keyboard Enter and phone touch follow the actual native fragment to the existing Windows safe-preparation heading. No Back/reload or installer execution.

pixel_review.observations: Four captures, three distinct byte identities, were opened. Desktop and phone show the complete changed Windows advice and command without page overflow; the phone visibly emphasises that a removed service is not running monitoring.
pixel_review.limitations: Synthetic offline browser surface; no native PowerShell/service, customer removal, credential-revocation, release or installation acceptance.

observer_limits: Initial fixture used a rewritten-document URL selector for a native same-page hash link; corrected without changing production navigation.

Chromium protocol response.body observed 91452 bytes with mojibake for a 91275-byte text/markdown response; WebKit protocol bytes and both actual consuming fetch ArrayBuffers match the entire 91275-byte source. Protocol mismatch remains retained, not source-byte proof.
